title: CHASE: Curiosity-Guided Skill Acquisition for Embodied Task Execution
abstract: arXiv:2611.34416v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Robots executing tasks in partially observed environments must resolve uncertainty while operating with incomplete skills. Inspired by human curiosity, we investigate how robots can formulate task-relevant hypotheses, seek evidence, and acquire missing skills during task execution. We propose CHASE, a Curiosity-guided Harness for Acquiring Skills from Evidence, which operationalizes curiosity as selecting investigations that resolve task uncertainty and expand executable capabilities. Four modules connect dynamic scene understanding, hypothesis-driven planning, on-demand skill acquisition, and verified execution. The planner balances information value, skill reuse, and acquisition/execution cost. Missing skills trigger bounded exploration, learning from verified segments, and held-out admission during acquisition; separate checks verify physical effects and acquired evidence. translated_title: CHASE：好奇心引导的具身任务执行技能习得
translated_abstract: 在部分可观测环境中执行任务的机器人，必须在使用不完整技能的同时解决环境中的不确定性问题。受人类好奇心的启发，我们研究了机器人如何在任务执行过程中提出与任务相关的假设、寻找证据并习得缺失的技能。我们提出了CHASE（Curiosity-guided Harness for Acquiring Skills from Evidence，基于证据的好奇心引导技能习得框架），该框架将好奇心具体化为选择能够解决任务不确定性并扩展可执行能力的调查行为。四个模块将动态场景理解、假设驱动规划、按需技能习得和经验证的执行连接起来。规划器在信息价值、技能复用以及习得/执行成本之间进行权衡。当出现缺失技能时，会触发有界探索、从经验证的片段中学习，以及习得过程中的保留集准入检验；独立的检查机制分别验证物理效果和所获得的证据。新准入的技能会扩展可执行的调查空间。
tldr: 该论文提出CHASE框架，将好奇心操作化为选择能够解决任务不确定性的调查行为，使机器人在部分可观测环境中能够提出假设、寻找证据并按需习得缺失技能，从而完成具身任务执行。
en_tdlr: CHASE operationalizes curiosity as selecting investigations that resolve task uncertainty, enabling robots in partially observed environments to formulate hypotheses, seek evidence, and acquire missing skills on demand during embodied task execution.
